strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#68187 by building pandas at buggy commit a547f69e8cfd, applying the PR's new tests to that tree, and running only the sparse accumulate tests. On the buggy revision Sparse[int64, nan] accumulations densify with to_dense(), so NA gaps become 0 and the dtype/value assertions fail. On the fixed revision the _densify() path keeps NaN gaps, promotes the subtype as the tests expect, and the tests pass.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) for building pandas Cython extensions

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py::test_accumulate_na_gaps_subtype_cannot_hold_na (parametrized over op_name in cumsum/cumprod/cummin/cummax and skipna in True/False) and pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py::test_accumulate_bool_subtype_promotes_to_object (parametrized over cumprod/cummin/cummax)
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on buggy a547f69e8cfd both new test functions fail for the affected cases, because result.dtype is Sparse[int64, nan] (or the wrong subtype) rather than the expected Sparse[float64, nan] or Sparse[object, nan], and/or the values are 0 where NaN is expected. On the fixed revision all parametrized cases pass, and the only int64-preserving case is cumsum with skipna=True, which takes the fast path.
strategy.numerical_probe: SparseArray([1.0, nan, 5.0, nan]).astype(SparseDtype('int64', nan)) wrapped in pd.Series, then cumprod/cummin/cumsum(skipna=False), compared after astype('float64') against the dense Series result.

input_output_examples.input: arr = pd.arrays.SparseArray([1.0, np.nan, 5.0, np.nan]).astype(pd.SparseDtype("int64", np.nan)); ser = pd.Series(arr); list(ser.cumprod())

risks: No platform or architecture is named in the evidence, so the defect is assumed to be platform-independent; if it only appears on a specific architecture or NumPy build, the transition may not occur on a generic Linux x86_64 host.

NumPy and the other dependencies have no documented constraint and no era ceiling (kind unbounded), so the NumPy version is chosen at install time and not pinned by evidence; a different NumPy major version could change the cast or warning behaviour.
Python version is not stated in the evidence; the pandas build chosen must support the Python version installed in the environment.

The RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in cast' may be promoted to an error by pytest filterwarnings configuration, which would change the failure mode on the buggy revision (error instead of wrong value) without changing the transition.

Do not compare results with to_dense() or sparse.to_dense() in any ad-hoc check, because they reproduce the same cast-the-gaps bug; the tests use astype('float64') and sparse.to_dense() only where the bool/object case requires it.
cumsum with skipna=True takes the numeric fast path and keeps int64, so it is not expected to fail on the buggy revision; this is a correct negative case, not a reproduction failure.
The test diff in the PR body references GH#68187 and the fix is unreleased, so there is no prior released behaviour to compare against; the buggy revision a547f69e8cfd must be checked out explicitly.

oracle.reference_source: dense pandas Series accumulation of the same values in the test itself (pd.Series(values) with np.nan)
oracle.why: Values are small exact integers and NaN positions; the reference is the dense computation, so exact equality after astype('float64') is appropriate.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On a547f69e8cfd the sparse result for Sparse[int64, nan] has subtype int64 (for cumprod/cummin/cummax) and gap values 0, so result.dtype == SparseDtype('float64', nan) fails before values are compared; for the bool test, the buggy result is not SparseDtype(object, nan), so the dtype assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, _accumulate uses _densify(), which promotes the NaN fill value with maybe_promote, so the result dtype is SparseDtype('float64', nan) (or object for bool) and values equal the dense Series computation with NaN gaps; all parametrized cases pass, with cumsum skipna=True keeping int64.
